business_model.claim: NRP earns revenue by owning, managing, and leasing a portfolio of mineral properties (primarily coal, oil and gas) to mining companies in the United States, collecting royalties and lease payments.
quotes: We are a diversified natural resource company engaged principally in the business of owning, managing and leasing a diversified portfolio of mineral properties in the United States, including interests in coal and other natural resources and own a non-controlling 49% interest in Sisecam Wyoming LLC ("Sisecam Wyoming"), a trona ore mining and soda ash production business.

business_model.claim: NRP reports three segments: Mineral Rights (approximately 13 million acres of mineral interests), Soda Ash (49% equity interest in Sisecam Wyoming), and Corporate and Financing (no revenue; bears interest and overhead costs).
quotes: Mineral Rights—consists of approximately 13 million acres of mineral interests and other subsurface rights across the United States.

competitive_position.claim: NRP operates a royalty-based mineral-rights business, owning and leasing a diversified portfolio of mineral properties across the United States rather than operating mines directly.
quotes: We are a diversified natural resource company engaged principally in the business of owning, managing and leasing a diversified portfolio of mineral properties in the United States, including interests in coal and other natural resources and own a non-controlling 49% interest in Sisecam Wyoming LLC ("Sisecam Wyoming"), a trona ore mining and soda ash production business.

competitive_position.claim: The Mineral Rights segment covers approximately 13 million acres of mineral interests that, if combined, would span roughly 20,000 square miles.
quotes: Mineral Rights—consists of approximately 13 million acres of mineral interests and other subsurface rights across the United States. If combined in a single tract, our ownership would cover roughly 20,000 square miles.

competitive_position.claim: NRP's revenue is concentrated among a small number of coal lessees: Alpha's mining operations accounted for approximately 26% of total revenues, Foresight approximately 21%, and Alabama Kanu's Oak Grove operation approximately 11% in 2025.
quotes: We own significant interests in several of Alpha's mining operations, which accounted for approximately 26% of our total revenues in 2025. We also own significant interests in all of Foresight's mining operations, which accounted for approximately 21% of our total revenues in 2025. We also own a significant interest in Alabama Kanu's Oak Grove operation, which accounted for approximately 11% of our total revenues in 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Sisecam Wyoming, in which NRP holds a 49% non-controlling interest, is described as one of the world's lowest-cost producers of soda ash.
quotes: Soda Ash—consists of our 49% non-controlling equity interest in Sisecam Wyoming, one of the world's lowest-cost producers of soda ash, an essential ingredient in the manufacturing of glass, solar panels, detergents, and batteries for electric vehicles.

competitive_position.claim: As of September 30, 2026, NRP's leverage ratio was 0.1x, it held $51.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, and it had $200.0 million of available borrowing capacity under its Opco Credit Facility.
quotes: ended the quarter with $251.7 million of liquidity consisting of $51.7 million of cash and cash equivalents and $200.0 million of available borrowing capacity under our Opco Credit Facility. As of September 30, 2026 our leverage ratio was 0.1 x.

competitive_position.claim: NRP fully repaid the remaining $13 million balance on its Opco Credit Facility during the third quarter of 2026, eliminating revolving debt and enabling a significantly increased Q3 2026 distribution of $2.34 per common unit.
quotes: We fully repaid the remaining $13 million balance on our Opco Credit Facility during the third quarter of 2026. As a result and consistent with our communications throughout the year, the Partnership was able to significantly increase the distribution with respect to the third quarter of 2026. In November 2026, the Board of Directors declared a distribution of $2.34 per common unit with respect to the third quarter of 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Natural gas is the primary competing fuel for thermal coal in power generation, and low natural gas prices combined with renewable energy gains have caused utilities to switch away from coal, depressing thermal coal prices.
quotes: Natural gas is the primary fuel that competes with thermal coal for power generation, and renewable energy sources continue to gain market share in power generation. The abundance and ready availability of cheap natural gas, together with increased governmental regulations on the power generation industry has caused a number of utilities to switch from thermal coal to natural gas and/or close coal-powered generation plants.

competitive_position.claim: Metallurgical coal pricing is tied to global steel demand, and NRP expects continued pricing pressure as soft global demand for steel persists.
quotes: Metallurgical coal pricing improved in the third quarter of 2026, however, we expect continued pressure on pricing as soft global demand for steel persists.

competitive_position.claim: The soda ash market is significantly oversupplied due to new capacity from China growing faster than global demand, and NRP does not expect to receive distributions from Sisecam Wyoming until the market returns to equilibrium through capacity rationalization.
quotes: The soda ash market continues to be significantly oversupplied from the influx of new capacity from China and sales prices remain below the cost of production for most producers. We expect soda ash prices to remain at these lower levels for the foreseeable future and do not expect distributions from Sisecam Wyoming to resume for several years until high-cost capacity is forced to retire.

competitive_position.claim: Climate change legislation, EPA emissions rules (including MATS), and the shift to natural-gas-fired and renewable power plants are expected to continue reducing coal consumption and NRP's coal-related revenues.
quotes: The adoption of climate change legislation and regulations restricting emissions of greenhouse gases and other hazardous air pollutants has resulted in changes in fuel consumption patterns by electric power generators and a corresponding decrease in coal production by our lessees and reduced coal-related revenues.

competitive_position.claim: Bankruptcies and mine closures in the coal industry pose a material risk to NRP, as rejected leases would cease operations and NRP would be unlikely to recover full rejection damages.
quotes: To the extent our leases are rejected, operations on those leases will cease, and we will be unlikely to recover the full amount of our rejection damages claims. More of our lessees may file for bankruptcy in the future, which will create additional uncertainty as to the future of operations on our properties and could have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Chinese tariffs on U.S. coal implemented in 2025 could continue to negatively affect coal prices and reduce the royalties NRP receives from its lessees.
quotes: the Chinese tariffs on U.S. coal, which were implemented in 2025, could continue to negatively affect the overall price of coal. If new legislation or additional trade restrictions are adopted or geopolitical tensions were to increase and reduce the price received by our lessees for coal sales, the amount of royalties that we receive from our lessees would also be reduced which could adversely affect our free cash flow.

competitive_position.claim: NRP's lease structure includes minimum royalty provisions that provide a floor on revenue even when production or prices decline.
quotes: For these types of leases, the lessees generally make payments to us based on the greater of a percentage of the gross sales price or a fixed price

competitive_position.claim: NRP's partnership agreement requires the consolidated leverage ratio to be less than 3.25x in order to make quarterly distributions in excess of $0.45 per unit, a covenant that NRP currently satisfies with wide margin at 0.1x leverage.
quotes: Our partnership agreement requires our consolidated leverage ratio to be less than 3.25x in order to make quarterly distributions on the common units in an amount in excess of $0.45 per unit.

competitive_position.claim: NRP's Mineral Rights segment revenues and other income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $149,142 thousand, a 4% decrease from the prior year period, while the Soda Ash segment recorded a loss of $(16,859) thousand from equity in loss of Sisecam Wyoming.
quotes: Revenues and other income during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 decreased $6.7 million, or 4%, as compared to the prior year period primarily due to lower thermal coal revenues, production lease minimum revenues, property tax revenues, and gains on asset sales, partially offset by higher metallurgical coal revenues, override royalty revenues and processing and transportation revenues.
